# DNSResolve-Termux

[![KernelSU](https://img.shields.io/badge/KernelSU-Compatible-green.svg)](https://kernelsu.org/)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Android](https://img.shields.io/badge/Platform-Android-green.svg)](https://www.android.com/)

**A KernelSU module that provides `/etc/resolv.conf` on Android so Go binaries inside Termux can resolve DNS.**

## Problem

Go-based CLI tools (crane, gh, docker CLI, etc.) use the Go resolver, which reads `/etc/resolv.conf` directly. On Android:

- There is no `/etc/resolv.conf` (it's a ramdisk rootfs, read-only)
- Termux keeps its own resolver under `$PREFIX/etc/resolv.conf`, which Go **never reads**
- Result: Go binaries fail with `lookup example.com on [::1]:53: connection refused`

## Solution

This module adds a `resolv.conf` via the standard KernelSU overlay mechanism:

```
/etc -> /system/etc   (Android symlink)
```

The module ships `system/etc/resolv.conf`, which KernelSU overlays onto `/system/etc`. Because `/etc` is a symlink to `/system/etc`, the file automatically appears at `/etc/resolv.conf` — where the Go resolver looks.

**Android's own DNS (netd/DnsResolver) is NOT affected** — it never reads this file.

## DNS servers

```
nameserver 8.8.8.8
nameserver 8.8.4.4
nameserver 1.1.1.1
```

Edit `system/etc/resolv.conf` inside the module to customize.

## Requirements

- Android with KernelSU (Next) — Magisk should also work via the fallback installer
- Termux

## Installation

1. Download the release zip from [Releases](../../releases)
2. KernelSU Manager (or Magisk app) → Modules → Install from storage
3. Reboot
4. Verify:

```sh
cat /etc/resolv.conf          # should show 3 nameservers
# or check module log
cat /data/local/tmp/dnsresolve.log
```

## Verification

After reboot, test with any Go binary:

```sh
# Before: fails with [::1]:53 connection refused
./crane digest alpine:latest

# After: resolves fine
./crane digest alpine:latest
# sha256:28bd5fe8b56d1bd048e5babf5b10710ebe0bae67db86916198a6eec434943f8b
```

## How it works

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `module.prop` | Module metadata for KernelSU/Magisk |
| `system/etc/resolv.conf` | The DNS file — overlaid to `/system/etc`, visible at `/etc` via symlink |
| `post-fs-data.sh` | Logs & verifies the overlay at boot |
| `customize.sh` | KernelSU installer |
| `META-INF/com/google/android/` | Magisk-compatible installer fallback |

## License

MIT
